what_this_is: The first revalidation of the ten complete five-link chains against a producer whose emitted IR had moved. Every chain fixture in crates/clean-verify/tests/fixtures pins its body's emitted trust-ir VERBATIM and link 2a asserts the registered spec module encodes the same graph — but the gate reads the FIXTURE, never a live dump, so nothing in this repo could tell whether the producer still emits it. This record is that comparison, run.
the_risk_this_tested: trust wave-DZ (3a09adfea2, merged 2026-08-18) changed emitted IR: a zero-displacement field access that used to lower to a bare `ret %0` now lowers to `const i64 0; gep inbounds i8, ptr %0, %1; ret %2`. Its own merge measurement: 101 of 13,774 clean-kernel rows moved, +286 instructions, 143 new GEP sites. If any chained body were among those 101 its committed fixture would be stale and its link-2a gate would be asserting against an IR the producer no longer emits.
the_answer: No chained body drifted. Stated at the strength it was MEASURED, which is not quite the strength the question was asked at: this lane did not reproduce wave-DZ's own 101-row A/B, because its subject is trust origin/main (6819d58406), four days and several lanes PAST wave-DZ's control -- vtable slices 6/10/11/12, the pass-1 splice refusals, #197 item 3c. On that wider A/B the delta is far bigger than 101: 9,321 of 13,075 common rows moved, 236 of them in instr_count, net +2,828 instructions. What is measured directly, body by body, is the claim that matters: zero instructions moved in any of the ten, zero `gep` appears in any of them, and every instr_count is unchanged. The inference that none is among wave-DZ's 101 rests on one further measured fact, its own: all 101 were ALREADY `derived_mir: unsupported` at wave-DZ's control, and every chained body is `agreed`. All ten still hold links 1 / 2b / 2c at HEAD — `agreed`, `markers_exact: true`, `unsupported: []`, zero calls, flip fired, and flip-event lineage == coverage-row lineage on 221/221 events crate-wide with 0 foreign events and 0 unjoinable. The designated target `level::Level::is_zero` is unchanged too: still `agreed`, still `markers_exact: false`, still NO flip event — the wall stands.
what_DID_move: Only whole-crate NUMBERING, in three token classes, none of which is an instruction: `functy.N` in the function header (all ten), `enum.N` / `struct.N` type-table ids (from_source_system, flat_flags_contains, expr_path_step_clone), and `@func.N` callee ids (level_is_zero only). These indices renumber whenever clean-kernel gains or loses an item OR the producer changes how many bodies it lowers, so they were ALREADY stale against the 2026-08-16 pre-wave-DZ dump.
attribution_ab: A producer-only A/B settles which side moved them: the SAME clean tree (6d84131c7) compiled with the pre-wave-DZ driver (trust 304ec590ca) and with the post-wave-DZ driver (trust 6819d58406). Same three token classes move, ZERO instructions move. So the drift is the producer's numbering, not clean-kernel source and not wave-DZ's GEP change. Field by field it is sharper still: across 13,075 common coverage rows the eleven chained bodies move in `func_id` ALONE -- not instr_count, not lowered, not spliced, not unsupported, not calls, and NOT `lineage` (which moved on 3,504 other rows). The chained bodies' lineage digests are stable under this producer change; they moved between the two CLEAN trees, which is what makes them a per-build identity rather than a producer signature. Two chains GAINED: from_source_system and flat_flags_contains go interpreter `not-run/0` -> `agreed/12` and `agreed/25`, so flat_flags_contains.lineage.json's pinned `not-run` is superseded by an improvement, not a regression.
why_the_fixtures_are_NOT_refreshed: Refreshing them would go RED in exactly two places, and that was measured by doing it: copying all eleven live bodies over the fixtures and running the gate gives 57 passed / 2 failed — `expr_path_step_clone_proved_module_matches_the_emitted_artifact` on the const-type lane (emitted enum176 vs the registered `ir_ep_tstep := IRTy.enum_ 181`) and `level_is_zero::is_not_transcribed_and_the_wall_stands` on a hard-coded `assert!(body.contains("call @func.4914"))`. Making those green again means moving a kernel-checked spec declaration for a token the semantics provably does not consult — a re-record, and one that would be stale again on the next clean-kernel commit. The re-DERIVATION is registered instead: `ir_ty_is_agg_enum_any` and `ir_ty_is_agg_struct_any` (spec/core_spec/eval_ir_ops.rs) prove `ir_ty_is_agg (IRTy.enum_ n) = true` for EVERY n, which is the only way the type reaches the machine (`ir_const_agg_eval` consults it and nothing else). The index is therefore a NAME, and that is now kernel-checked rather than asserted in a comment.
what_nothing_checked_before_this: NOTHING in the repo compares a chain fixture to a live dump. Confirmed by exhaustion: the only trustc-invoking scripts are scripts/trust_ir_build.sh (whole-crate axis ratchet, touches no fixture) and scripts/trust_verify_ratchet.sh (a different mechanism); the perturbation batteries and scripts/crystal_lane_matrix_battery.sh MUTATE the fixtures to prove lanes discriminate but never re-derive them; verify_runner has no trustc row; there is no hook or workflow that does it. `crystal_a1_lineage.rs`'s own module doc already says the lineage digest is RECORDED and not recomputed, and level_is_zero.a0.json says a stale digest 'is invisible to every test in the repo'. The IR TEXT had no such statement anywhere. scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py is the mechanism that was missing.
